title: Intaspecific aggression assay for Nylanderia fulva
author: Edward Lebrun
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8z9hx96
materials: 0 | Ants come in contact and part.

steps.title: Select bait stations and collect ants
steps.instruction: Identify each bait station that recruited Nylanderia fulva (Nf). Test each station against its two nearest‑neighbor stations; also test the first and last stations against each other. Replicate every pairing three times, giving six aggression trials per bait card (minimum 30 workers per station). Collect ants from each selected station within 24 h of collection and never conduct trials after sunset or before dawn.

steps.title: Prepare holding tubs
steps.instruction: Place collected workers in small tubs that are NOT fluon‑coated. Add a wet paper towel and a cotton ball soaked with 30 % sugar solution. Avoid any alien food, perfumed detergents, or other artificial odor sources. Prepare one extra tub of ants from each nest to serve as negative‑control ants.

steps.title: Prepare fluon‑coated arena vials
steps.instruction: Use 20 mL clear glass scintillation vials (5.5 cm height × 2.5 cm diameter). Coat the walls with Fluon™ except for the bottom 1 cm, which must remain clear for observation. Ensure a band of Fluon is present 1 inch from the vial bottom for ant removal.

steps.title: Set up assay environment
steps.instruction: Place a warming mat set to 30 °C in the observation area. Tape white paper to the mat to provide a white background for the arena vials. Keep all vials (both isolated and waiting to be combined) on the warming mat throughout the assay.

steps.title: Assign observer and organizer roles
steps.instruction: Two people must work together: the Observer (blind to ant identity) and the Organizer (who tracks vial codes and prepares pairings). The Observer should wear magnifying glasses, avoid breathing on vial openings, and may use a dust mask.

steps.title: Collect workers into sugar‑soaked tubs
steps.instruction: Using a phorid aspirator or a paint brush, transfer workers from each nest into the prepared small tubs with the 30 % sugar source. Collect an additional tub from one nest to serve as the negative‑control group.

steps.title: Transfer ants to arena vials
steps.instruction: With a small paint brush (or a phorid‑type aspirator used gently), remove ants from the holding tubs and place them into the fluon‑coated arena vials. Do not include dead ants, males, brood items, or queens. If an aspirator is used, employ a screened vial that is dedicated to a single tub (do not reuse screened vials across tubs).

steps.title: Label and code vials
steps.instruction: The Organizer assigns a unique code to each arena vial and records the true identity of the ants inside. Keep a master list linking codes to colony/source information.

steps.title: Acclimate ants in vials
steps.instruction: Allow ants to adjust in their isolated arena vials for at least 10 minutes but no more than 20 minutes before pairing. Keep the vials on the 30 °C warming mat during this period; prolonged isolation beyond 20 minutes may cause stress.

steps.title: Combine paired vials to start assay
steps.instruction: When the acclimation period is complete, tip one arena vial into its paired vial on the warming mat. Transfer the code tape from the empty vial to the newly combined vial so the Observer remains blind to identity.

steps.title: Observe and record aggression
steps.instruction: Do not observe the combined vial for the first minute. Then observe every 2 minutes (at 1, 3, 5, and 7 minutes after combination). During each observation watch the arena for exactly 20 seconds and record the most aggressive interaction seen, using the 0‑to‑5 qualitative aggression scale (0 = no interaction, 5 = formic‑acid spray or ball fighting). Include optional positive (known aggressive) and negative (known non‑aggressive) control pairs in each assay set when possible.

steps.title: Clean and store vials for reuse
steps.instruction: After each assay, clean vials either (a) with non‑perfumed detergent and warm water followed by re‑fluon coating, or (b) preserve the fluon by wiping the bottom with an ethanol‑moistened cotton swab, then a water‑moistened swab, and finally drying with a clean swab. Place cleaned vials in a warm location (e.g., drying oven) and do not reuse them for at least 24 hours to allow drying and volatilization of any residues.
